# Argonaut Labs

> Independent measurements of frontier-scale open-weight models streamed from NVMe on one machine: Kimi K3.1 Pro on one 96 GB RTX PRO 6000, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 on a single 128 GB Apple M5 Max MacBook Pro.

Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T, 1.45 TB of experts), one 96 GB RTX PRO 6000: 3.79 tok/s decode on raw text with a Qwen drafter that keeps the answer identical, prefill up to 43 tok/s, contexts up to 16,384 tokens with K3.1's sparse attention. Standard tests, 11 November 2026, commit bb5c53b (tag k31-cuda-20261111), four NVMe devices, fresh process per run, greedy, raw prompts, drafter on / off: tg128 on "The three main financial statements are" (6 tokens) decode 2.76 / 2.06-2.07 tok/s; pp512 / tg200 prefill 15.7-15.9 tok/s, decode 3.88-3.89 / 1.55 tok/s; pp1512 / tg128 prefill 40.4-40.8 tok/s, decode 2.92 / 1.71 tok/s; the same 6-token prompt with 512 generated, decode 3.77-3.79 / 1.97 tok/s. Against the 10 November release on the same drives (3.21 and 2.98 tok/s on the two long tests), long predictable text decodes 18 to 30% faster with the drafter, because a verification block may take up to 64 rows; a code prompt, everyday prompts, chat and plain decode are unchanged; every compared position has the same logits as the 10 November release (4,747), and the drafter's 2,639 logit vectors are identical to plain decoding. On 8 November, with a fifth NVMe, prefill reached 18.0 tok/s at 512 tokens and 43 tok/s at 1,512. Chat runs at about 2 tok/s. Long context: a 6,769-token prompt takes about 56 s at an 8k cache and decodes at 1.53-1.54 tok/s; a 13,167-token prompt takes about 115 s and decodes at 1.56-1.57 tok/s. The spine's activations are fp32 since 8 November. On a MacBook Pro M5 Max (128 GB, Metal, tag k31-metal-20261111) the same release decodes the 512-generated test at 2.49 tok/s with the drafter, against 1.99 with the 9 November settings in the same session (2.29 against 1.81 with the laptop in use). Code and caveats: https://github.com/argonautlabsai/argodrive-ds4-kimi-k3.1

Earlier, on the M5 Max. Key numbers (workloads, timing definitions and output comparisons differ by experiment; see the linked evidence):
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q4 (518 GB), our ds4 fork vs pinned upstream ds4 on the same single internal SSD: prompt processing 16.12 -> 43.75 (2.71x), steady decode 10.18 -> 18.66 (1.83x, 27 Sept session). With two Thunderbolt 5 NVMe enclosures: 68.29 prompt tokens/s and 22.25 decode (23.26 at 512 generated).
- Kimi K3 (2.78T), deltafin fork: 0.55 tok/s on the internal SSD, 0.96 with three enclosures on the public 17-token prompt; 1.00 steady over 512 generated tokens on four drives.
- GLM-5.3 (744B, 434 GB at 4-bit), ds4 fork: 2.02 tok/s on the internal SSD, 3.70 with three enclosures; a scheduling change measured +15 to +16%.

## Which software runs Kimi K3.1 Pro?

Argodrive DS4 Kimi K3.1 is the integrated Linux/CUDA inference engine, not an add-on to install alongside upstream ds4. Its repository includes the Kimi port, NVMe streaming, expert caches and weight-preparation tools. Users build this repository and download the model checkpoint separately. NVIDIA/CUDA build dependencies are required. There is currently no prebuilt installer. The separate Argodrive Mac monitoring app is not required.

## Start here
- [Install and run Kimi K3.1 Pro — step-by-step guide](https://argonautlabs.ai/guides/install-kimi-k31.html): build the integrated engine, download Moonshot’s original checkpoint, extract experts, convert the spine, then run a local completion. Includes copyable Linux commands, storage planning and troubleshooting.
- [Get Argodrive DS4 Kimi K3.1 — the inference engine](https://github.com/argonautlabsai/argodrive-ds4-kimi-k3.1): an experimental single-GPU port built on Antirez’s ds4. Tested on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with 96 GB VRAM, 70 GiB VM RAM and four or five NVMe devices. Contexts up to 16,384 tokens tested with K3.1's sparse attention; reference-model equivalence has not been validated. The separate Argodrive Mac app is not required.
- [Build and setup](https://argonautlabs.ai/research/kimi-k31-single-gpu.html#reproduce): pinned release, weight preparation links and reproduction limits.

## Pages
- [Apple silicon benchmark archive](https://argonautlabs.ai/research/apple-silicon-results.html): complete earlier drive ladders and charts for Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4.1 and GLM-5.3; all original measurements retained.
- [Run Kimi K3.1 Pro locally on one GPU](https://argonautlabs.ai/research/kimi-k31-single-gpu.html): November 6–11 measurements, drafter results, long context with sparse attention, NVMe layout, pinned CUDA build, metric definitions and reference-validation limits.
- [DeepSeek V4.1 stack, drive ladder, prefill follow-ups](https://argonautlabs.ai/research/deepseek-2026-09-27.html): method, levers, every arm, 30 September prefill qualification.
- [DeepSeek V4.1 prefill experiment, 15 September](https://argonautlabs.ai/research/deepseek-2026-09-15.html)
- [GLM-5.3 scheduling experiment](https://argonautlabs.ai/research/glm.html)
- [Home: Kimi K3.1 Pro, the earlier models and the Argodrive Mac app](https://argonautlabs.ai/)
